cards.front: In bacteria, which enzyme removes the RNA primers during DNA replication?
cards.back: **DNA polymerase I**. Its **5'→3' exonuclease** activity removes each RNA primer, and it fills the gap with DNA. **DNA ligase** then seals the remaining nick. DNA polymerase III makes most of the new strand.
cards.back_pt: A **DNA polimerase I**. Sua atividade de **exonuclease 5'→3'** remove cada primer de RNA, e ela preenche a lacuna com DNA. A **DNA ligase** então sela a quebra (*nick*) restante. A DNA polimerase III sintetiza a maior parte da nova fita.

cards.front: What do topoisomerases do during DNA replication, and which drugs block them?
cards.back: They cut and rejoin DNA to relieve **supercoiling** ahead of the replication fork. **Fluoroquinolones** block two bacterial type II topoisomerases: **DNA gyrase** and topoisomerase IV. In cancer therapy, **irinotecan** blocks human topoisomerase I and **etoposide** blocks human topoisomerase II.
cards.back_pt: Elas cortam e religam o DNA para aliviar o **superenrolamento** à frente da forquilha de replicação. As **fluoroquinolonas** bloqueiam duas topoisomerases bacterianas do tipo II: a **DNA girase** e a topoisomerase IV. Na terapia do câncer, o **irinotecano** bloqueia a topoisomerase I humana e o **etoposídeo**, a topoisomerase II humana.

cards.front: How does telomerase keep chromosome ends from shortening?
cards.back: Telomerase is a **reverse transcriptase** that carries its own **RNA template**. It adds **TTAGGG** repeats to the **3' end** of the chromosome. This makes up for the DNA lost at the end of the lagging strand in each round of replication.
cards.back_pt: A telomerase é uma **transcriptase reversa** que carrega seu próprio **molde de RNA**. Ela adiciona repetições **TTAGGG** à **extremidade 3'** do cromossomo. Isso compensa o DNA perdido no fim da fita descontínua (*lagging strand*) a cada ciclo de replicação.

cards.front: What does mismatch repair fix, and what happens when it fails?
cards.back: It fixes **mispaired bases** and small insertion-deletion loops that DNA polymerase leaves in the **newly made strand**. Defects (e.g., **MLH1**, **MSH2**) cause **microsatellite instability** and **Lynch syndrome** (hereditary colorectal and endometrial cancer).
cards.back_pt: Corrige **bases mal pareadas** e pequenas alças de inserção-deleção que a DNA polimerase deixa na **fita recém-sintetizada**. Defeitos (ex.: **MLH1**, **MSH2**) causam **instabilidade de microssatélites** e **síndrome de Lynch** (câncer colorretal e de endométrio hereditários).

cards.front: How are DNA double-strand breaks repaired, and which diseases involve this pathway?
cards.back: **Nonhomologous end joining** joins the broken ends directly; it is fast but can lose bases. **Homologous recombination** copies the sister chromatid and is accurate; it needs **BRCA1/BRCA2**. **ATM** senses the breaks; its loss causes **ataxia-telangiectasia**.
cards.back_pt: A **junção de extremidades não homólogas** une as pontas quebradas diretamente; é rápida, mas pode perder bases. A **recombinação homóloga** copia a cromátide-irmã e é precisa; depende de **BRCA1/BRCA2**. A **ATM** detecta as quebras; sua perda causa **ataxia-telangiectasia**.

cards.front: How do silent, missense, nonsense and frameshift mutations differ?
cards.back: **Silent**: new codon, same amino acid. **Missense**: a different amino acid (e.g., sickle cell, glutamate→valine). **Nonsense**: an early **stop codon**. **Frameshift**: an insertion or deletion that is not a multiple of 3 changes every codon after it.
cards.back_pt: **Silenciosa**: códon novo, mesmo aminoácido. **De sentido trocado** (*missense*): outro aminoácido (ex.: anemia falciforme, glutamato→valina). **Sem sentido** (*nonsense*): **códon de parada** precoce. **Deslocamento da fase de leitura** (*frameshift*): inserção ou deleção que não é múltipla de 3 altera todos os códons seguintes.

cards.front: Which three steps turn eukaryotic pre-mRNA into mature mRNA in the nucleus?
cards.back: A **5' 7-methylguanosine cap**, a **3' poly-A tail**, and **splicing** out of introns by the **spliceosome** (snRNPs plus proteins). **Anti-Smith antibodies** target snRNP proteins and are highly specific for SLE.
cards.back_pt: **Cap (capuz) de 7-metilguanosina** na extremidade 5', **cauda poli-A** na extremidade 3' e **splicing** (remoção dos íntrons) pelo **spliceossomo** (snRNPs e proteínas). Os **anticorpos anti-Sm** (anti-Smith) reconhecem proteínas das snRNPs e são altamente específicos do LES.

cards.front: How do DNA methylation and histone acetylation change gene expression?
cards.back: **Methylation** of cytosines in **CpG islands** near promoters **silences** genes. **Histone acetylation** removes the positive charge of lysines, loosens chromatin and **activates** transcription; deacetylation does the opposite. Neither changes the DNA sequence.
cards.back_pt: A **metilação** de citosinas em **ilhas CpG** perto dos promotores **silencia** genes. A **acetilação de histonas** neutraliza a carga positiva das lisinas, afrouxa a cromatina e **ativa** a transcrição; a desacetilação faz o contrário. Nenhuma das duas altera a sequência do DNA.

questions.stem: A 2-year-old boy of Italian descent has had pallor and poor growth since he was 8 months old. He needs regular red cell transfusions. Exam shows frontal bossing and splenomegaly. Hemoglobin is 6.1 g/dL, and mean corpuscular volume is 58 fL. Hemoglobin electrophoresis shows very little HbA and a high HbF. Sequencing of both beta-globin genes shows the same single-base change inside intron 1. The exon sequences are normal. What is the most likely effect of this mutation?
choices: One amino acid in beta-globin is replaced by another
Transcription of the beta-globin gene is blocked at the promoter
Abnormal splicing leaves part of the intron in the mature mRNA
The beta-globin mRNA does not receive a 5' cap
Beta-globin chains are made but cannot bind heme
questions.explanation: This is **beta-thalassemia major**. A base change inside an intron can create a new **splice site**, so the spliceosome leaves part of the intron in the mature mRNA. The abnormal mRNA usually contains an early stop codon, so little normal beta-globin is made. A missense mutation (as in sickle cell disease) changes a codon inside an exon, but here the exons are normal.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **beta-talassemia maior**. Uma troca de base dentro de um íntron pode criar um novo **sítio de splicing**, e o spliceossomo deixa parte do íntron no mRNA maduro. O mRNA anormal geralmente contém um códon de parada precoce, então pouca beta-globina normal é produzida. Uma mutação de sentido trocado (como na anemia falciforme) altera um códon dentro de um éxon, mas aqui os éxons são normais.

questions.stem: A 9-year-old girl is brought to a dermatologist. Since infancy she has had severe sunburns after very short sun exposure. Her face and arms have many dark freckles and areas of dry, thin skin. A crusted nodule on her nose is biopsied and shows squamous cell carcinoma. Her parents are first cousins. Her cultured skin fibroblasts die much more easily than normal cells after ultraviolet light exposure. Which DNA repair process is most likely defective?
choices: Base excision repair
Mismatch repair
Nonhomologous end joining
Homologous recombination
Nucleotide excision repair
questions.explanation: This is **xeroderma pigmentosum**, an autosomal recessive defect in **nucleotide excision repair**. UV light makes **pyrimidine dimers** that distort the helix; normally endonucleases cut out the damaged segment, and DNA polymerase and ligase fill the gap. Base excision repair is the tempting choice, but it removes single damaged bases that do not distort the helix, not UV dimers. Mismatch repair defects cause Lynch syndrome, not sun sensitivity.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **xeroderma pigmentoso**, um defeito autossômico recessivo do **reparo por excisão de nucleotídeos**. A luz UV forma **dímeros de pirimidina** que distorcem a hélice; normalmente endonucleases cortam o segmento lesado, e a DNA polimerase e a ligase preenchem a lacuna. O reparo por excisão de bases é a alternativa tentadora, mas remove bases lesadas isoladas que não distorcem a hélice, e não dímeros causados por UV. Defeitos do reparo de erros de pareamento causam síndrome de Lynch, e não sensibilidade ao sol.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man comes to the emergency department with severe vomiting and watery diarrhea. Twelve hours earlier he ate wild mushrooms that he picked in a forest. He improves with intravenous fluids. Two days later he becomes jaundiced and confused. ALT is 4,800 U/L, and INR is 3.4. The toxin responsible most likely inhibits which enzyme in his hepatocytes?
choices: RNA polymerase I
RNA polymerase II
RNA polymerase III
DNA polymerase delta
Peptidyl transferase of the 60S ribosomal subunit
questions.explanation: Death cap mushrooms (*Amanita phalloides*) contain **alpha-amanitin**, which strongly inhibits **RNA polymerase II**. Without new mRNA, hepatocytes die, causing **acute liver failure** after a period of apparent improvement. RNA polymerase III is blocked only at much higher toxin levels, and RNA polymerase I is resistant. Rifampin, by contrast, blocks the bacterial RNA polymerase.
questions.explanation_pt: Cogumelos *Amanita phalloides* contêm **alfa-amanitina**, que inibe fortemente a **RNA polimerase II**. Sem mRNA novo, os hepatócitos morrem, causando **insuficiência hepática aguda** após um período de melhora aparente. A RNA polimerase III só é bloqueada em concentrações muito maiores da toxina, e a RNA polimerase I é resistente. A rifampicina, por outro lado, bloqueia a RNA polimerase bacteriana.

questions.stem: A 4-year-old boy is evaluated for clumsy walking. He started walking at 13 months, but over the past year his gait has become wide-based and unsteady. He has had pneumonia three times and frequent sinus infections. Exam shows truncal ataxia and small dilated blood vessels on the white of both eyes. Serum IgA is low, and alpha-fetoprotein is high. His cultured cells show many chromosome breaks after x-ray exposure. Which protein is most likely defective?
choices: ATM, a kinase that signals DNA double-strand breaks
XPA, a protein of nucleotide excision repair
MLH1, a protein of DNA mismatch repair
BRCA2, a protein of homologous recombination
Frataxin, a mitochondrial iron-handling protein
questions.explanation: This is **ataxia-telangiectasia**, an autosomal recessive defect in **ATM**. ATM senses **DNA double-strand breaks** and starts repair and cell-cycle arrest, so the cells are very sensitive to **ionizing radiation**. Cerebellar ataxia, eye telangiectasias, IgA deficiency with sinopulmonary infections and a high AFP are the classic clues. Friedreich ataxia (frataxin) is the tempting choice, but it starts later, usually in adolescence, and causes no immune deficiency or telangiectasias.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **ataxia-telangiectasia**, um defeito autossômico recessivo da **ATM**. A ATM detecta **quebras de fita dupla do DNA** e inicia o reparo e a parada do ciclo celular; por isso, as células são muito sensíveis à **radiação ionizante**. Ataxia cerebelar, telangiectasias oculares, deficiência de IgA com infecções sinopulmonares e AFP elevada são as pistas clássicas. A ataxia de Friedreich (frataxina) é a alternativa tentadora, mas começa mais tarde, geralmente na adolescência, e não causa imunodeficiência nem telangiectasias.

notes.title: Molecular biology: replication, repair, gene expression and protein fate
notes.body_md:
## DNA replication

- Starts at an **origin** (one in bacteria, many in eukaryotes). **Helicase** unwinds the DNA; single-strand binding proteins keep the strands apart.
- **Primase** makes an RNA primer. **DNA polymerase III** (bacteria) extends it 5'→3' and proofreads 3'→5'.
- **DNA polymerase I** removes primers; **ligase** joins Okazaki fragments.
- **Topoisomerases** relieve supercoiling (**fluoroquinolones** block the bacterial type II ones). **Telomerase** extends chromosome ends.

## DNA repair

- **Nucleotide excision**: cuts out bulky lesions such as UV **pyrimidine dimers**; defect = **xeroderma pigmentosum**.
- **Base excision**: glycosylases remove single damaged bases (e.g., deaminated cytosine).
- **Mismatch repair**: fixes replication errors; defect = **Lynch syndrome**.
- **Double-strand breaks**: nonhomologous end joining or homologous recombination (**BRCA1/2**).

## Transcription and RNA processing

- Eukaryotic **RNA polymerase I** makes most rRNA, **II** makes mRNA, **III** makes tRNA. **Alpha-amanitin** blocks polymerase II; **rifampin** blocks the bacterial RNA polymerase.
- **Promoters** (e.g., TATA box) sit just upstream of the gene; **enhancers** can act from far away.
- Pre-mRNA gets a **5' cap** and a **poly-A tail**, and its introns are **spliced** out.

## Translation

- **Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases** load the correct amino acid onto each tRNA, using ATP.
- Starts at **AUG** (methionine). Elongation uses GTP. A **stop codon** is read by a release factor.
- Bacterial ribosomes are **70S** (30S + 50S); eukaryotic ones are **80S** (40S + 60S). Many antibiotics use this difference.

## Gene regulation

- **Lac operon**: on when **glucose is low** (cAMP-CAP binds) and **lactose is present** (the repressor lets go).
- **DNA methylation** silences genes; **histone acetylation** activates them. Imprinting depends on methylation.

## Protein fate

- **Chaperones** (heat shock proteins) help proteins fold.
- Misfolded proteins get **ubiquitin** tags and are destroyed by the **proteasome** (blocked by bortezomib).
- The Golgi adds **mannose-6-phosphate** to lysosomal enzymes; without it, **I-cell disease** results.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Replicação do DNA

- Começa em uma **origem** (uma nas bactérias, muitas nos eucariotos). A **helicase** desenrola o DNA; proteínas de ligação à fita simples mantêm as fitas separadas.
- A **primase** produz um primer de RNA. A **DNA polimerase III** (bactérias) o estende no sentido 5'→3' e revisa no sentido 3'→5'.
- A **DNA polimerase I** remove os primers; a **ligase** une os fragmentos de Okazaki.
- As **topoisomerases** aliviam o superenrolamento (as **fluoroquinolonas** bloqueiam as bacterianas do tipo II). A **telomerase** estende as extremidades dos cromossomos.

## Reparo do DNA

- **Excisão de nucleotídeos**: retira lesões volumosas, como os **dímeros de pirimidina** causados por UV; defeito = **xeroderma pigmentoso**.
- **Excisão de bases**: glicosilases removem bases lesadas isoladas (ex.: citosina desaminada).
- **Reparo de erros de pareamento**: corrige erros da replicação; defeito = **síndrome de Lynch**.
- **Quebras de fita dupla**: junção de extremidades não homólogas ou recombinação homóloga (**BRCA1/2**).

## Transcrição e processamento do RNA

- Nos eucariotos, a **RNA polimerase I** produz a maior parte do rRNA, a **II** produz mRNA e a **III** produz tRNA. A **alfa-amanitina** bloqueia a polimerase II; a **rifampicina** bloqueia a RNA polimerase bacteriana.
- Os **promotores** (ex.: TATA box) ficam logo antes do gene; os **enhancers** (*amplificadores*) podem agir à distância.
- O pré-mRNA recebe um **capuz 5'** e uma **cauda poli-A**, e seus íntrons são removidos por **splicing**.

## Tradução

- As **aminoacil-tRNA sintetases** ligam o aminoácido correto a cada tRNA, usando ATP.
- Começa no **AUG** (metionina). O alongamento usa GTP. Um **códon de parada** é reconhecido por um fator de liberação.
- Os ribossomos bacterianos são **70S** (30S + 50S); os eucarióticos são **80S** (40S + 60S). Muitos antibióticos exploram essa diferença.

## Regulação gênica

- **Operon lac**: ativo quando a **glicose está baixa** (cAMP-CAP se liga) e a **lactose está presente** (o repressor se solta).
- A **metilação do DNA** silencia genes; a **acetilação de histonas** os ativa. O imprinting depende de metilação.

## Destino das proteínas

- As **chaperonas** (proteínas de choque térmico) ajudam as proteínas a se dobrar.
- Proteínas mal dobradas recebem marcas de **ubiquitina** e são destruídas pelo **proteassomo** (bloqueado pelo bortezomibe).
- O Golgi adiciona **manose-6-fosfato** às enzimas lisossômicas; sem ela, surge a **doença da célula I**.
